fields.statement: rhiza inbox is the owner's one list of what waits on them across a repo's runs: questions with a recommendation, sign-offs and failed runs, with a Rex notification for each.

fields.acceptance: A testscript with fixture journals of a run blocked on a question, a run waiting at sign-off, a failed run, a run interrupted again after a daemon resume and a done run lists exactly the first four in order in text and --json; once the question is answered, the sign-off approved, the given-up run abandoned and a new fake run started and finished on the failed run's change set, rhiza inbox says nothing waits and lists no failed run for the abandoned one.
fields.statement: rhiza inbox lists, oldest first across every run of the repo, each item waiting on the owner with a short item ID: a question (its run, change set, session tab and the question), a run waiting at sign-off, a failed run (its failed step and detail, until it is retried with rhiza run resume --retry or a newer run starts on its change set), and a run the daemon gave up on (interrupted again after the daemon's one resume, its step, until it is resumed or abandoned), in text and --json, and says so when nothing waits. A run failed by rhiza run abandon is the owner's own act and is never listed as a failed run.

fields.acceptance: A testscript with a fake Rex opens a question item and sees the asking session's tab focused, opens a sign-off item and sees the run's tab focused, and gets exit 2 for an unknown item.
fields.statement: rhiza inbox open <item> focuses the Rex tab of the session that asked a question, or of the run for a sign-off, a failed run or a run the daemon gave up on, so the owner answers in the agent's own menu; an unknown item exits 2.

fields.acceptance: A testscript with a review run waiting at sign-off approves it through its inbox item and finds the run done with an approved entry, sends another back with one finding and finds a fix cycle started, and gets exit 2 approving a question item; describe-golden is regenerated.
fields.statement: rhiza inbox approve <item> and rhiza inbox request-changes <item> <file> act on a sign-off item through rhiza run approve and rhiza run request-changes on that item's run, and exit 2 on any other kind of item.

fields.acceptance: A testscript with a fake adapter whose agent blocks on a question finds an advisor launched with that question, its recommendation journalled and shown by rhiza inbox, no message sent to the asking session and the run still blocked; with a failing fake advisor the item shows no recommendation and the run is still blocked.
fields.statement: When a normal run blocks on a question, the engine launches a short-lived advisor session (the arbiter's guide in recommend-only mode) that reads slice and why for the question and journals a recommendation with its reasons, never answering it; the run does not wait for the advisor, the inbox shows the recommendation beside the question, and a failed advisor leaves the question without one.

fields.acceptance: With a fake Rex, a run that blocks on a question, then waits at sign-off, another that fails and a third the daemon gives up on send exactly four notifications, one per item, and none while each item stays in the inbox.
fields.statement: Each new inbox item sends one Rex notification naming the change set and what waits (a question, a sign-off, a failed run or a run the daemon gave up on), through the blocked-run notice path, and none again while the item stays.

This change set's intent still reads 'Genesis watches runs and passes their questions to the owner, with a recommendation drawn from slice and why', but answers 4, 7 and 16 made it the whole inbox: sign-offs approved or sent back, failed runs and runs the daemon gave up on, and a notification for each. No rhiza command restates a change set's intent. Should the intent be restated (which needs a way to do it), or should the sign-off and failed-run leaves move to a new change set whose intent covers them?

ops.note: the inbox capability whose leaves fall outside the change set's intent as written

fields.statement: Plan review round 3 left finding f2 (missing-acceptance on inbox-notify): needs is empty, yet its acceptance covers 'a third [run] the daemon gives up on' and counts notifications per inbox item. A given-up run comes from daemon-resume-once (another change set), and what makes an inbox item, and when it stays or leaves, is defined by inbox-list. Built first, as needs [] allows, the check can't run. It needs inbox-list (which already needs daemon-resume-once). The critic confirmed it: inbox-notify has no needs, yet its statement ('each new inbox item') and its acceptance (four items: a question, a sign-off, a failed run and a run the daemon gave up on, with no repeat while each stays) rely on inbox-list to say what an item is and when it stays, and on daemon-resume-once for the given-up run. Built first, as an empty needs allows, the check has nothing to run against. It needs inbox-list, which already needs daemon-resume-once. How should it be settled?

Plan review round 3 left finding f3 (contradiction on inbox-notify): It sends each notification 'through the blocked-run notice path', but that path is in the run process: Engine.Notify -> runRex.notice in internal/api/run.go:1482, called only from block/unblock in internal/run/engine.go:862,879. A run the daemon gave up on is interrupted, so no run process is left to notify. That item, and any item the daemon or the inbox spots after the fact, needs a sender outside the run, which neither the leaf nor the daemon leaves name. The critic confirmed it: The blocked-run notice path is in the run process. reportToRex sets Engine.Notify to runRex.notice (internal/api/run.go:1461-1500), which writes an OSC 7501 record to the run's own terminal, and the engine calls it only on block and unblock (internal/run/engine.go:885-889). A run the daemon gave up on is interrupted, so its process is gone and nothing can send that item's notice. No leaf gives the daemon or the inbox its own sender, so inbox-notify's acceptance can't be met for that item as written. How should it be settled?

Plan review round 3 left finding f4 (contradiction on inbox-open): It focuses 'the Rex tab ... of the run for a sign-off, a failed run or a run the daemon gave up on', but no record holds a run's tab. The journal keeps tabs only for blocked sessions (Block.TabSession/TabWindow/TabBlock in internal/run/journal.go:200), run-process-record journals only host and pid, and daemon-run-tabs doesn't journal the tab it opens. A leaf has to record the run's tab (or inbox-open has to name another target), or this part of the acceptance has nothing to focus. The critic confirmed it: The journal keeps a tab only in Block (TabSession/TabWindow/TabBlock, internal/run/journal.go:198-206), for a session blocked on the owner. Started has no tab (journal.go:175-190), run-process-record journals only host and pid, and daemon-run-tabs doesn't say it journals the tab it opens. inbox-open's acceptance focuses 'the run's tab' for a sign-off, and its statement does the same for failed and given-up runs, but nothing records that tab. A leaf has to journal the run's tab, or inbox-open has to name another target. How should it be settled?
